content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Draw and interpret complete reaction profiles
Identify activation energy, enthalpy change, and transition state
Compare catalysed and uncatalysed reaction profiles
Use reaction profiles to explain reaction behaviour

(also called energy profile diagrams) show how energy changes throughout a reaction. They are more detailed than simple energy level diagrams because they show the activation energy and the transition state.

Explain, using a reaction profile, how a catalyst increases reaction rate without changing the products formed.
A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway
This pathway has a lower activation energy (lower peak on profile)
Therefore ΔH and the products are the same
But more particles have enough energy to overcome the lower barrier
More successful collisions occur per second
Measuring Eₐ from products instead of reactants
Eₐ is always from reactants to the peak (transition state)
Thinking the transition state is a real compound
The transition state is unstable and exists only momentarily
Drawing catalysed pathway with different start/end points
Only the peak height changes; reactants and products are the same
